mcq.q: A railway network stores station information in a doubly linked list. A train moves from one station to another, both forward and backward. If a station is closed and removed from the middle of the list, what should be done?

options.A: The previous station’s next pointer should be updated AND The next station’s previous pointer should be updated
options.B: The next station’s previous pointer should be updated
options.C: The train must restart from the first station
options.D: A new list must be created

mcq.answer_text: The previous station’s next pointer should be updated AND The next station’s previous pointer should be updated

mcq.q: What is the minimum number of pointers required to maintain a doubly linked list
A Least Recently Used (LRU) cache is implemented using a doubly linked list, where recently accessed items move to the front. What happens when a new item is accessed, and the cache is full?

options.A: The least recently used item is removed
options.B: The new item is added at the front
options.D: The most recently used item is deleted

mcq.answer_text: The least recently used item is removed

mcq.q: A web browser keeps track of visited pages using a doubly linked list. The user can go back and forward through the history. What will happen if the user presses the "Back" button?

options.A: The current pointer moves to the previous node

mcq.answer_text: The current pointer moves to the previous node

mcq.q: What happens if you try to traverse a doubly linked list from the head to tail

options.A: Only the next pointer is used
options.B: Both next and previous pointers are used
options.C: The traversal is not possible without the tail pointer
options.D: The list must be converted into an array first

mcq.answer_text: Only the next pointer is used

lq.q: Consider y ou are developing a photo album manager application. Each photo in the album is represented as a node in a doubly linked list. The application should support the following features: Add Photo: Insert a new photo into the album at any specific position Remove Photo: Remove a photo from the album by its ID. Move Photo: Move a photo to a different position in the album. Display Album: Display all photos in the album in their current order. How would you implement these functionalities using a Doubly linked list? Each node will represent a photo, and it will have the following fields: photoID: A unique integer identifier for each photo. prev: A pointer to the previous node in the list. next: A pointer to the next node in the list.
